findings.locator: Josef Fuchs, 'The Absoluteness of Moral Terms', 1971, translated/reprinted in 1979 at pp. 117–125
findings.document_finding: Author distinguishes premoral harms from moral evil and judges concrete actions within intention and circumstances; first-hand statement now cited, unlike former purely Roman criticism.
findings.qualification: Direct comparison with 1971 Gregorianum typesetting and other original proponents still pending.

findings.locator: Fuchs, 1979 reprint pp. 118–125, 'The So-Called Exceptions to the Norm', 'Moral and Premoral Evil', 'Intrinsece Malum?'
findings.document_finding: Fuchs explains why killing described materially differs from murder and why surgical harm can belong to healing; he rejects a simple universal category without specifying action and ends.
findings.qualification: Should not flatten him to simple utilitarianism or an advocate of conscience as unlimited autonomy.

findings.locator: Fuchs, reprint pp. 119–125, reason for excluding fully material universal descriptions
findings.document_finding: First-hand proponent text makes it possible to specify disputed description of the moral object, rather than attack mere consequences in the abstract.
findings.qualification: Fuchs' interpretation of moral objects remains disputed; no theological certification is asserted.

findings.locator: Germain Grisez, Anthropotes (1985), Moral Absolutes: A Critique of the View of Josef Fuchs, S.J., introduction
findings.document_finding: A published first-person Catholic critic explicitly defends exceptionless negative norms against Fuchs, distinct from Grisez's 1973 unpublished manuscript.
findings.qualification: Author-hosted published document identified and introductory extract reviewed; detailed 1985 page-by-page collation pending.

findings.locator: John Paul II, Veritatis splendor §§75–83, proportionalism and intrinsically evil acts
findings.document_finding: Original magisterial text criticises the claim that aggregate goods may override an intrinsically wrong chosen object.
findings.qualification: This is the responding magisterium, not the original proponent's own position.

findings.locator: Fuchs, original 1971 essay reprint pp. 109–125, objective recta ratio and historically conditioned rules
findings.document_finding: Fuchs explicitly cares about objective moral truth and raises questions about universal norms in changed circumstances.
findings.qualification: His views are one documented strand, not the whole of pre- or postconciliar moral theology.

findings.locator: Fuchs reprint pp. 110–112, concrete conscience judged against recta ratio
findings.document_finding: Author's position treats conscience as judging concrete reality under objective reason; cannot be represented as an unqualified licence to invent morality.
findings.qualification: Whether its theory adequately protects intrinsically wrong objects remains contested.

findings.locator: Fuchs reprint pp. 117–125, premoral good and concrete norms
findings.document_finding: The named, original pre-1993 proponent argument can now be contrasted with Veritatis splendor directly.
findings.qualification: The debate remains larger than Fuchs; another original proponent is needed for complete representative coverage.

findings.locator: Preparatory draft De fontibus revelationis, 1962, chapter I §§3–6, Komonchak English translation 2012, pp. 2–3
findings.document_finding: The text really uses a twofold-source formula and states claims about Tradition and the Magisterium.
findings.qualification: The read witness is a scholarly English translation of the proposed 1962 original; Latin-original typeset collation is not yet complete.

findings.locator: Original preparatory scheme, chapter I §§3–6, presented on 14 November 1962
findings.document_finding: The original draft articulates apostolic transmission and twofold sources; it is a preparatory draft rather than the final Council constitution.
findings.qualification: The document itself cannot attest all voting interventions or later motivations.

findings.locator: Karl Rahner, Disquisitio brevis de schemate De fontibus revelationis, PUC Chile manuscript archive Caja 7 Carp 2 Doc 14
findings.document_finding: Institutional manuscript catalogue attributes to Rahner criticisms of length, pastoral character and ecumenical orientation.
findings.qualification: Only the catalogue abstract was examined; do not quote or certify the unreviewed 11MB manuscript.

findings.locator: Synopsis of Dei Verbum textual development, Italian preface footnote 1, p. I, chronology for 14–21 November 1962
findings.document_finding: The synoptic history records the contested draft and the fact that the vote to interrupt debate missed a two-thirds majority before John XXIII assigned work to the mixed commission.
findings.qualification: The vote counts 1,368/822/19 come from the historical chronology; the underlying roll-call/Acta are not yet independently collated.

findings.locator: Vatican II Dei Verbum §§9–10, original promulgated text
findings.document_finding: Final text describes a common divine wellspring, one sacred deposit, and the Magisterium as servant of the word.
findings.qualification: A theological allegation of contradiction needs full contextual comparison; the words alone do not establish it.

findings.locator: 1962 draft chapter I §4 twofold source and §6 Magisterium
findings.document_finding: Unlike the final constitution, the draft explicitly uses twofold-source vocabulary and calls the Magisterium the proximate universal norm for belief.
findings.qualification: Difference in terminology does not by itself show that final Vatican II denied apostolic Tradition.

findings.locator: Italian synopsis preface footnote 1, mixed-commission papal intervention
findings.document_finding: Procedural outcome cannot be described simply as the Council abolishing an approved dogma in a successful two-thirds vote.
findings.qualification: The full Acta Synodalia and interim versions are needed to determine individual motives.

findings.locator: University archive summary of original Rahner 1962 manuscript, Latin outline in title record
findings.document_finding: A known critic's actual archival work is identified, with explicit pastoral and ecumenical objections catalogued.
findings.qualification: Original Rahner manuscript pages were not read; details beyond the abstract remain uncertified.

findings.locator: Pius XII Humani generis, 1950, critique of swapping fixed dogma for fluctuating philosophical concepts
findings.document_finding: Pius XII warns against identifiable novel theological methods independently of the specific 1962 revelation schema.
findings.qualification: The warning does not prove Rahner personally advocated each condemned method.

findings.locator: Fuchs reprint pp. 120–125, premoral harms and moral absolutes
findings.document_finding: The response explicitly keeps Fuchs's own appeal to practical reason while defending intrinsically evil objects against reduction to outcomes.
findings.qualification: A complete fair doctrinal assessment still requires expert theology review, not just citations.

outstanding: Fuchs's original 1971 Gregorianum print has not been line-by-line collated with the full 1979 Curran–McCormick reprint; direct selections were reviewed in the reprint.
Grisez's 1985 published original reply has been identified; further detailed passage and his published exchange with Fuchs remain to be independently reviewed.
Rahner's authentic Latin Disquisitio manuscript is catalogued, but not directly inspected; only the archival abstract establishes the three general objections noted.
1963–65 intermediate Council schemas, complete Acta Synodalia debates, and the original 1962 Latin print require full collation before assigning detailed redrafting motives.
Neither the existence of a proponent document nor the differences between draft and final constitutes independent doctrinal, legal or native French publication approval.
